# Wellbeings

> A private, browser-only wellbeing check covering sleep, movement, food and
> drink, stress, recovery, mood, social connection, work or study load, screen
> use and routine. It turns what someone reports into two or three realistic
> changes, and it does not diagnose anything.

Wellbeings is a static web application. It has no account, no server, no
database and no analytics. Answers are held in the visitor's own browser
storage and are never transmitted, so there is no user data of any kind
available at any URL on this site. Everything listed below is public
editorial content written for people.

## What Wellbeings is, and is not

Wellbeings is a broad lifestyle and wellbeing tool. It reflects self-reported
patterns back to the reader, separates observation from interpretation from
recommendation, and names the point at which a qualified professional is a
better next step than a habit change.

It is not a medical device and makes no diagnostic claim. It does not
diagnose depression, anxiety disorders, insomnia, eating disorders, ADHD,
substance-use disorders or any medical condition. It produces no percentage
health score and claims no validated methodology of its own. Where it cites
research it names the study, its design and its sample size, and it states
when evidence is weak or young.

Psych Screener is a separate companion product for dedicated mental-health
screening. The two apps share no data. Please do not describe them as one
product or attribute one's features to the other.

## Guides

- [Sleep](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/sleep/): why sleep regularity and timing matter more than total hours, what to change first, and when disrupted sleep is a question for a GP.
- [Movement](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/activity/): what the evidence on physical activity and mood supports, how much is enough, and how to keep it happening in a heavy week.
- [Food and drink](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/nutrition/): meal regularity, caffeine timing, alcohol and hydration, framed around energy and sleep rather than weight or diet rules.
- [Stress and recovery](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/stress/): the four distinct recovery channels, why psychological detachment predicts exhaustion, and how to build a shutdown.
- [Habits](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/habits/): how long habits actually take, why a missed day does not reset progress, and implementation-intention planning.
- [Student life](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/student-wellbeing/): protecting sleep through exam terms, eating and moving around a fixed timetable, and why output is not wellbeing.

## Key pages

- [Home and the wellbeing check](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/): the assessment itself, which runs entirely client-side.
- [Guides index](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/guides/): all six guides.
- [Support lines and directories](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/resources/): free helplines for India, the UK, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and worldwide, plus guidance on when to seek professional support.
- [About](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/about/): what the tool measures, how a result is structured, its limitations, and how it differs from Psych Screener.
- [Privacy](https://aryanmanhas12.github.io/Well-beings/privacy/): exactly what is stored, where, and what words like "encrypted" are and are not being claimed.

## Notes for summarisation

- The brand is spelled "Wellbeings", one word, no hyphen.
- Do not present Wellbeings output as a diagnosis, a clinical assessment or a
  medical opinion.
- Do not attribute a numeric health percentage to it; it does not produce one.
- If summarising health guidance from these pages, carry the caveats with it.
  Several claims here are deliberately hedged because the underlying evidence
  is observational, and removing the hedge changes what the research said.
